correctness.rationale: The center and leaf ball averages give the stated gradient map with μ=(Σg_i)/(m+1). Every gradient vector is realizable by positive data by raising the center baseline. Put a=1/(m+1). On an affine cell with center selector zero, column j has magnitude at most 1 in row j and a in every other row. With center selector μ the diagonal magnitude is at most 1−a and the other rows are still bounded by a. Multiplication by w_i and division by w_j gives the stated global bound by partitioning a line segment at the selector hyperplanes, with continuity for ties. At the displayed witness the center selects zero, the distinguished minimum-weight leaf selects itself, and all other leaves select μ=−a/2. A positive increment smaller than 1/2 has output gradient increments exactly t at that leaf and at each other leaf at; this realizes the bound. For one leaf the relative output is g_1/2 for either sign. With fixed W the bound for m≥2 is strictly decreasing in w_min, so equal weights uniquely minimize it. In the signed example the initial difference is constant but every output edge-gradient difference has magnitude 1/2+a. Perturbing one leaf of h by t makes the denominator w_1|t| and the numerator tend to W(1/2+a). The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its formal-mask and finite data tests are not needed for the universal proof.
